newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open mostly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open mostly unchanged.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open mostly unchanged Wednesday based on market orders at 1017 EDT, traders said.
Tuesday, December cotton closed 0.39 cent higher at 75.41 cents a lb after trading from 75.45 to 74.75 cents. The rest ended up 0.25 to 0.47.
The October contract closed at a 0.02 cent premium to December compared with a 0.05 cent premium in December the previous day.
An estimated 5,100 lots changed hands on the day.
Analysts expect trade to remain thin ahead of the U.S. Department of Agriculture's monthly supply and demand estimates, released August 12.

The weather across much of the cotton belt, meantime, is mostly favorable for crop development. Bolls are beginning to open in the south of Texas while steady growth has been noted in California and Arizona, Weather Services Corp said.
In the Delta, the crop is developing closer to average after heavy rains set the cotton off to a slow start earlier in the season.
